subject: BUSINESS CONTRACT APPROVAL REQUEST: Core overlay first slice
body:
Business lane requests Master approval/sign-back for the Core-contract first slice before implementation.

PLAN SUMMARY
Implement a narrow Core-owned overlay contract first, then let Business adapt to it. Core remains the public install/update/runtime source of truth. Business remains a private standalone overlay at /Users/sem/code/ArgentOS-Business and must never be imported by Core startup unless entitlement, manifest, signature/checksum, and Core-version checks pass.

LICENSE EXPIRATION POLICY
Preserve Business data and installed artifact, disable Business execution/surfaces, keep Core fully usable, and allow renewal/reactivation without data loss. Active licenses may enable verified Business descriptors/runtime. Offline-within-grace remains enabled as status=grace but does not fetch private updates unless entitlement sync succeeds. Expired licenses disable Business import/runtime/surfaces and preserve data/artifact. Revoked or invalid licenses hard-disable immediately with no grace, preserve data, and redact all private license/package details. Manual disable behaves like expired and remains non-destructive. Default offline grace: 72 hours.

CORE C1: EXTENSION API TYPES
Add a public-safe @argentos/core-extension-api surface with type-only contracts for overlay manifest metadata, entitlement status, tool descriptors, gateway handler descriptors, dashboard panel/widget descriptors, docs roots, migration preview metadata, and lifecycle hooks onEnable/onDisable/health. No Business imports.

CORE C2: MANIFEST VALIDATOR
Validate business-overlay.json metadata and descriptors only. Support dev-mode validation of /Users/sem/code/ArgentOS-Business/business-overlay.json and runtime installed manifests. Produce structured validation errors. Never evaluate/import the entrypoint. Reject incompatible Core versions, missing required entitlements, unsafe/unknown fields where applicable, and private URLs in public status output.

CORE C3: ENTITLEMENT AND OVERLAY STATUS STORE
Define statuses: none, active, grace, expired, revoked, invalid, disabled, error. Store redacted public state only: org id/name, tier, entitlements, expiry, grace deadline, last sync, installed overlay version, enabled flag, redacted error state. Do not expose raw license keys, private package URLs, registry coordinates, or private protocol payloads. Business owns encrypted private license payloads/protocol details.

CORE C4: GATEWAY STUBS
Add business.status, business.activate, business.sync, and business.disable. status returns public-safe entitlement/install/enabled/expiry/grace/error information. activate accepts a key, uses existing licensing/download mechanism, verifies package/manifest, and enables only if active. sync refreshes entitlement/update metadata and applies expiration/revocation state. disable hides Business runtime/surfaces without deleting data.

CORE C5: DESCRIPTOR REGISTRY
Register descriptor placeholders for tools, gateway methods, dashboard panels/widgets, docs roots, and migration previews. Only load Business executable code after entitlement, signature/checksum, manifest, and Core-version gates pass. Expired/revoked/invalid states expose no executable Business handlers. First slice does not apply Business migrations and does not run Business worker/governance code.

BUSINESS B1 AFTER CORE API EXISTS
Business may then adapt /Users/sem/code/ArgentOS-Business to compile against the Core extension API, replace Core-relative imports with Business DTOs and injected Core facades, and remain descriptor-only for the first Business wave. No worker runtime, governance runtime, or migration apply until the contract is proven.

TEST PLAN
Core boots with no Business overlay installed. Good business-overlay.json validates without importing Business code. Bad/incompatible manifests reject without import. business.status redacts secrets and private coordinates. Active license enables verified descriptors. Expired license disables Business tools/routes/workers while preserving data and Core behavior. Revoked license disables immediately with no grace. Offline grace keeps Business enabled only until grace deadline. business.disable hides surfaces without deleting data. argent update updates Core always, updates Business only when entitlement is active or grace-valid, and skips private fetches when expired/revoked.

REQUEST
Please approve/sign back this contract, amend it, or assign the Core owner/task ID for C1-C5. Business lane will remain read-only until Master explicitly authorizes code work.

Operator direction: continue AppForge 2.0 toward Airtable/TableForge. Immediate ask is to task AppForge so phases 1, 2, 3, and 4 become usable, real, and truthful.

Current truthful status:
- Overall against full Airtable-class/TableForge spec: about 15%.
- Against internal single-user table-builder MVP: about 35-45%.
- Recent workflow unblock slice is ready in branch codex/appforge-core-readiness commit 20b74a32: appforge-core catalog entry, installState metadata-only, Workflows readiness read_ready, not write_ready.

What is done/foundation:
- AppForge desktop modal and left nav exist.
- Core model exists for bases/tables/fields/records/revisions.
- Gateway methods exist for appforge.bases.*, appforge.tables.*, appforge.records.*.
- Postgres storage schema exists for appforge_bases/appforge_tables/appforge_records/appforge_idempotency_keys.
- Basic grid/table editing exists.
- Basic field model supports text, long_text, single_select, multi_select, number, date, checkbox, url, email, attachment placeholder, linked_record placeholder.
- Canonical workflow events exist: forge.table.created/updated/deleted, forge.record.created/updated/deleted, forge.review.requested/completed, forge.capability.completed via workflows.emitAppForgeEvent.

What is stubbed/preview only:
- Kanban/form/review/interface/automation/connector/permissions/activity/settings surfaces are not all live product features yet.
- Permissions have model/helper coverage but are not full end-to-end enforcement.
- Interfaces are preview/generated surfaces, not a real editable interface designer.
- Automations point to Workflows but are not a full Airtable automation builder inside AppForge.
- Connector/import/sync is mostly product intent and metadata, not complete execution.

Not done versus Airtable/TableForge:
- Airtable-grade grid: keyboard nav, paste/fill, frozen columns, polished cell editors, large table behavior.
- Durable saved views with shared filters/sorts/groups/hidden fields.
- Formula, lookup, rollup, linked-record UX, attachments, relationship handling.
- Real interface designer.
- Forms with conditional logic/public sharing.
- Full permissions/audit/collaboration/version history.
- Import/export parity and AI/NL base creation/editing.
- Live workflow template enablement against guaranteed seeded AppForge bases/tables.

Recommended next Threadmaster task breakdown:

Phase 1 - Workspace MVP stabilization:
Goal: dependable single-user AppForge table builder.
Deliver: create base, create/rename/delete/duplicate tables, field CRUD, record CRUD, persistent active base/table/view/field state, honest empty/error states, browser smoke.
Acceptance: operator can create a base, add tables/fields/records, close/reopen, and keep state through gateway-backed storage.

Phase 2 - Core data domain hardening:
Goal: make gateway/AppForge store the source of truth instead of UI metadata fallback.
Deliver: finish server-method contracts for base/table/field/view/record operations; confirm Postgres ensure/migration path; revision/idempotency conflicts; compatibility path for legacy metadata apps.
Acceptance: base/table/record CRUD is durable and conflict-safe; Workflows can resolve real base/table ids from appforge.bases.list and appforge.tables.list.

Phase 3 - Airtable-quality grid and saved views:
Goal: make the table editor feel usable daily.
Deliver: saved views, durable filters/sorts/groups/hidden fields/field order, field-specific editors, stable columns, row selection, keyboard nav first pass.
Acceptance: user can create multiple saved views per table, switch them, and see predictable data changes without localStorage-only truth.

Phase 4 - Generated editable interfaces:
Goal: turn bases into usable mini apps, not just tables.
Deliver: interface metadata model, generated grid/form/detail/review/dashboard pages, basic interface editor panel, field/action binding, capability declaration editor.
Acceptance: every base can generate a form, detail page, review queue, and dashboard summary; edits persist without changing table schema.

Coordination boundaries:
- AppForge owns dashboard/src/components/AppForge.tsx, dashboard/src/components/app-forge/**, dashboard/src/hooks/useForgeStructured*.ts, src/infra/app-forge-*.ts, src/gateway/server-methods/app-forge*.ts, src/agents/tools/app-forge-tool*.ts, AppForge-specific ops docs.
- Coordinate before touching workflow runtime/canvas files, AOS connectors, OpenClaw, schema/migrations, package/version/release.
- Workflows consumes AppForge only through metadata/events/gateway methods; no UI/runtime imports.

Requested master direction:
1. Approve next AppForge lane as Phase 1+2 first, then Phase 3, then Phase 4, or split parallel subagents by phase.
2. Confirm whether AppForge should rename in code/docs now to TableForge/Argent Tables/Titan Table, or keep AppForge identifiers until product name is final.
3. Decide merge order for existing readiness branch codex/appforge-core-readiness commit 20b74a32 before new Phase 1-4 work.
4. Task AppForge with a concrete next slice; recommended first slice: gateway-backed base/table/record persistence smoke plus durable saved views seed, because that unlocks real operator testing and Workflows base/table resolution.

subject: REVIEW: Rust Sprint 2 Workflows scheduler/canary and rollback boundaries
body:

Workflows review response for task-20260501003535-ckanjr and task-20260501003536-5mmp5n. This is review-only guidance; no Rust implementation was performed.

Scheduler/canary stance:
- APPROVE the current Sprint 2 planning direction only if Rust remains shadow-only and Node remains live gateway/scheduler/workflow/timer/channel authority.
- BLOCK any Rust live timer, cron.add/cron.update, workflow schedule reconciliation, workflow wait resume, workflows.run dispatch, channel send, connector send, or workflow_runs/workflow_step_runs mutation until durable authority and duplicate-prevention gates exist.
- Workflows sees overlap with active live-readiness canary gating: Rust must not bypass Workflows liveReadiness/importReport/canary gates for imported workflows. Any future Rust workflow canary must exercise the same Node-owned policy surface or a byte-for-byte compatible shadow evaluator with no live side effects.

Safe fixture guidance:
- Safe now: read-only authority/status fixtures; protocol health/config/schema fixtures; copied/synthetic cron store comparisons; copied/synthetic workflow schedule reconciliation comparison; copied/synthetic waiting_duration/waiting_event due-time classification; formatter/report rendering.
- Safe with isolated state only: cron workflowRun fixture using an in-memory temp store and a synthetic inactive/test workflow row, asserting would-run/would-not-run without creating workflow_runs.
- Unsafe until later gates: live cron.add/cron.update/cron.run, live workflows.run, live resumeDueWorkflowWaits, live trigger of heartbeat/nudge/audio/channel/email/Slack/connector side effects.

Required isolated state before any workflow/scheduler canary:
- Temp cron store or in-memory store not shared with Node.
- Temp Postgres/schema copy or synthetic rows for workflows/workflow_runs/workflow_step_runs; never production tables.
- Deterministic nowMs and schedule inputs.
- Synthetic workflow IDs prefixed clearly as Rust shadow/canary fixtures.
- No access to live outbound deps, channel deps, connector deps, or agent dispatch deps.
- All emitted evidence must be would-create/would-resume/would-run, not started/running/completed.

Evidence that blocks live promotion:
- Any duplicate workflowRun cron job creation or stale-job removal mismatch.
- Any drift in nextRunAtMs/due-time classification versus Node.
- Any waiting_duration or waiting_event row that Rust would resume differently from Node.
- Any live side-effect route reachable from Rust during canary.
- Missing durable authority record with epoch, updatedBy, reason, and authority fields.
- Missing rollback dry-run that lists in-flight workflow runs, waiting steps, cron jobs, and ambiguous Rust-owned work.
- Missing proof that only one authority can execute a workflow/timer at a time.

Auth/token and rollback stance:
- Keep rollback read-only/design-only until a durable authority record exists. A mutating rollback command is blocked.
- Auth/token parity must prove Gateway auth behavior without logging or storing tokens in Rust reports. Tokens must be redacted, and Rust must not read model/provider auth profiles as part of workflow/scheduler parity.
- Rollback dry-run must enumerate in-flight workflow_runs with statuses created/running/waiting_approval/waiting_event/waiting_duration, current_node_id, workflowId/version, and source authority if known.
- Rollback dry-run must enumerate enabled workflowRun cron jobs and nextRunAtMs, plus any duplicate jobs for the same workflowId.
- Rollback dry-run must refuse success if both Node and Rust claim scheduler/workflowTimer/channel authority, if authority epoch is missing/stale, or if Rust-owned in-flight work cannot be mapped back to Node.
- Rollback must not mark runs failed/cancelled by default. For existing Node workflow semantics, waiting_* runs are legitimate durable states; rollback should preserve them and let Node resume through existing Node paths after authority is restored.

Recommended path for Rust:
1. Keep Sprint 2 as read-only reports plus isolated fixture comparisons.
2. Add an authority/status JSON contract first, with Node as current authority and Rust shadow-only.
3. Add duplicate-prevention tests using copied cron/workflow state.
4. Only after Workflows/AppForge/AOS reviews land should Rust propose a clean rebased packet with exact files and proof.

Workflows status note: active Workflows canary gating packet tm-20260501004200-l6ebzv blocks live imported workflow runs unless bindings/liveReadiness/canary proof are present. Rust must treat that as the current Workflows live policy.
